text:
Durchlauchtigſter Fürſt,
Gnädigster Fürst und Herr!
fuer Hochfürstlichen Durchlaucht worden durch den H.
H. Lombardini schon erfahren haben, daß ich das Geld
nicht sogleich in Breslau habe empfangen können und
noch ohne die großen Hinderniße der unbeschreiblichen Wege
und Wetters bin aufgehalten worden. Demohngeachtet
aber von Breslau aus meine Reise so beschleuniget, daß
den 25ten zu Mittag hier war und Honrichs u. Cabanis

noch angetroffen, welche dann auch, nachdem Honrichs
6000 f. und die Schenkungs Urkunden in original mit den
Frohesten Aussichten, noch denselben Tag abgefahren.
Den Herr K. R. von Triebenfeld befinden sich am rechtl. Arm
sehr leydend, doch haben Sie mir versprochen, so bald Sie nur
hier Ihre eigene Geschäften zur beendiget haben würden, sogleich
auf einigen Wochen nach Schlawentz zu kommen.
antworte
Nachdem hierüber aller erhaltenen Gnädigst Aufträgen werden erhalte
haben werdj ich eylen zurückzukommen.
In tiefsten Unterwerfung ersterben als
Euer Hochfürstlich Durchlaucht
Kontop
d. 26ten febr.
1810.
unterthänigst treu gehorsamte
Bally

translation.en: Most Serene Prince, Most gracious Prince and Lord! for Most Serene Highness will already have learned through Mr. Lombardini that I was not able to receive the money at once in Breslau, and, even apart from the great impediments of the indescribable roads and weather, was detained. Notwithstanding this, however, I so hastened my journey from Breslau that on the 25th at midday I was here, and still found Honrichs and Cabanis

still found here, who then also, after Honrichs [had received?] 6000 f. and the deeds of donation in the original, departed that same day with the most joyful prospects. The Herr Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld finds himself suffering severely in the right[?]/legal arm, yet he has promised me that as soon as he shall have concluded his own affairs here, he will come at once for some weeks to Schlawentz. I answer After all the most graciously received instructions concerning this shall have been received, I shall hasten to return. In deepest reverence I remain, until death, as Your Most Serene Highness's Kontop, the 26th of February 1810. most humble, faithful and most obedient Bally

text_english:
Most Serene Prince, Most gracious Prince and Lord! for Most Serene Highness will already have learned through Mr. Lombardini that I was not able to receive the money at once in Breslau, and, even apart from the great impediments of the indescribable roads and weather, was detained. Notwithstanding this, however, I so hastened my journey from Breslau that on the 25th at midday I was here, and still found Honrichs and Cabanis

still found here, who then also, after Honrichs [had received?] 6000 f. and the deeds of donation in the original, departed that same day with the most joyful prospects. The Herr Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld finds himself suffering severely in the right[?]/legal arm, yet he has promised me that as soon as he shall have concluded his own affairs here, he will come at once for some weeks to Schlawentz. I answer After all the most graciously received instructions concerning this shall have been received, I shall hasten to return. In deepest reverence I remain, until death, as Your Most Serene Highness's Kontop, the 26th of February 1810. most humble, faithful and most obedient Bally
summary_en: Reports, via Lombardini, that the money could not be collected at once in Breslau and that dreadful roads and weather delayed the journey; nonetheless the writer reached Kontop by midday on the 25th, still finding Honrichs and Cabanis there, who left the same day in high spirits after Honrichs received 6000 f. and the original deeds of donation. Notes von Triebenfeld's badly afflicted right arm and his promise to come to Schlawentz for some weeks once his business is concluded. Signed Bally.
summary_de: Bericht über die verzögerte Rückreise: Das Geld konnte in Breslau nicht sogleich empfangen werden, dazu behinderten unwegsame Straßen und schlechtes Wetter die Reise; dennoch traf der Schreiber am 25. mittags ein und fand Honrichs und Cabanis noch vor, die nach Übergabe von 6000 f. an Honrichs sowie der Schenkungsurkunden im Original noch am selben Tage zuversichtlich abreisten. Der Kriegs- und Forstrath von Triebenfeld leidet am rechten Arm, will aber nach Abschluß seiner hiesigen Geschäfte für einige Wochen nach Schlawentz kommen; um weitere Weisungen wird gebeten.
